21.0.0.en: Manasseh succeeded his father Hezekiah on the throne of Judah when he was twelve years old, and his reign lasted fifty-five years in Jerusalem. This was the longest period that any king sat on the throne of Israel or Judah, and his mother's name was Hephzibah.

21.0.1.en: This means that Hezekiah begat Manasseh three years after his healing and God's lengthening of his life, and perhaps he named him so because he felt that God had made him forget the illness and given him a new life and strong health. But sadly he became occupied with the world, in the form of his concern for the gifts that came to him from those who congratulated him, and was proud and displayed his possessions before the envoys of Babylon to boast of them, and he neglected the upbringing of his son Manasseh, who walked in evil and led the people of God astray more than all the kings who preceded him on the throne of Judah.

21.1.0.en: Manasseh did not follow the example of his father Hezekiah, and perhaps the motive for this was the encouragement of some of the leaders and counselors who loved the worship of idols, or perhaps his mother inclined to evil. What matters is that he walked in the way of evil and idol worship and all the abominations that the nations practiced, and so he led the people of God astray, because he submitted to the worship of the nations and did not learn that they were driven out of the land of Canaan because of their evils, and consequently he exposed himself and his people, by evil conduct, to distresses and to being driven out of this land. This indeed happened, for Manasseh was taken captive for a time to Babylon, and then, after a while, the Babylonian captivity of the people took place.

21.2.0.en: Sadly, he rebuilt the temples of the idols on the high places, which his father had torn down, and so he renewed evil in every place in Jerusalem and around it. Among these temples he set up altars for Baal, a famous pagan god. And he followed the evils of Ahab king of Israel and made a grove for the worship of the pagan gods whom they believed to dwell in heaven. In this he offered worship to the stars and the heavenly bodies and abandoned the worship of God.

21.3.0.en: And going further in evil, Manasseh dared with insolence to build altars to the pagan gods inside the house of the Lord, to challenge Him and provoke Him. Solomon had built altars for idols in Jerusalem, but Manasseh set them up inside the house of the Lord. Thus the temple was no longer a place for hallowing the name of God, but for the worship of idols.

21.4.0.en: He built altars for all the host of heaven and defiled the house of the Lord with them. He was not content with setting them up in the outer court of the temple, but brought them into the inner court of the priests, which no one was allowed to enter except the priests.

21.5.0.en: The host of heaven: the heavenly bodies, the stars and planets.

21.5.1.en: Used enchantments: sought to read the unseen, visions and dreams.

21.5.2.en: Observed times: seeing good or bad omens in certain persons, or numbers, or days.

21.5.3.en: Familiar spirits: the ancients used to believe that it was a spirit that answered the call of its owner, and they thought they were good spirits, whereas the familiar spirit is Satan.

21.5.4.en: The attendant spirit: a jinn, which some eastern peoples anciently believed followed a man wherever he went.

21.5.5.en: Manasseh went deep into the worship of idols, to the point of offering his son as a burnt offering to the pagan god Molech; he used sorcery and believed all the pagan beliefs, so he used enchantments, observed times and went after the demons that hide behind familiar spirits and attendant spirits. Thus he went on in every kind of evil to provoke God, and in this he violated the Law of God (Deut 18:

21.6.0.en: Manasseh also made an image of the grove, perhaps taking it from Assyria: a pillar adorned with goats' horns, with the figure of a palm tree on top of the pillar, in addition to a metal network on which were figures of palms, buds, pomegranates and sexual organs to arouse the passions. Then he set this image inside the house of the Lord. This shows the extent of his concern for the worship of the pagan gods and his challenge to God, because God had told David and Solomon to hallow this house for the glorifying of the name of God, but Manasseh made the house of the Lord for the glorifying of the pagan gods.

21.7.0.en: The Lord had made it a condition for His people, in order to keep them forever in the land that He gave to their fathers, that they should keep and do His commandments and the Law that Moses gave them.

21.8.0.en: But they did not listen, for Manasseh seduced them, so they increased in their evil even beyond the other nations whom the Lord drove out before Israel. For the nations did not know God, so they worshiped idols; but the people of God, after God had done great miracles with them and they had worshiped Him for many years, returned to the worship of the idols of the surrounding nations.

21.8.1.en: If you have repented of sins and moved away from them, do not be careless and return to them. For having tasted the sweetness of life with God, how can you return to evil and uncleanness?! Do not keep anything that brings you back to evil, and cut off your relationship with everyone who helps you in this. Remain firm in the life of repentance, that you may enjoy God.

21.9.s.en: (2) The warning to Manasseh and Jerusalem

21.9.0.en: Since Manasseh persisted in his evils and the worship of idols, God warned him through the prophets. God arranged that a large number of prophets should be contemporary with him: Isaiah, Hosea, Habakkuk, Nahum and Zephaniah. They would teach him, and if he did not accept, they would rebuke him, and then, as he continued in evil, they would declare God's judgment on him, that perhaps he might repent. But he went further in evil than the original inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, such as the tribes of the Amorites, and led his people astray, for he told them that the worship of these idols was worship of Jehovah, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. And he was cruel: he was not content merely to disregard the words of the prophets, but violently killed Isaiah, sawing him in two without mercy with a wooden saw, as Jewish tradition mentions, although Isaiah was related to him, being of the royal seed.

21.10.0.en: Tingle: his ears cannot bear it and are pained by the very loud sound.

21.10.1.en: Therefore the Lord declared His judgment, that He would permit a great calamity to fall upon Jerusalem and all Judah, so that everyone to whom news of this calamity came would not bear to hear the news, because of its cruelty.

21.11.0.en: The line: the string that the builder stretches along the wall to ensure that it is straight.

21.11.1.en: The Lord threatened him, saying: I will bring upon Jerusalem the punishment that I brought before upon Samaria and upon Ahab and his house, and I will wipe Jerusalem out of existence, as a dish is wiped of the remains of food and then turned upside down on its face, so that nothing remains in it. The stretching of the line here is, of course, for pulling down and not for building. We notice that God did not break the dish but emptied everything in it, for He loves His city Jerusalem and His people, and wants only to cleanse them of evil, that the remnant may repent and return to Him, so that He builds Jerusalem anew and brings them back from captivity.

21.12.0.en: And I will forsake the remnant of My people and deliver them into the hand of their enemies, so that they become captives and their enemies plunder them. By the remnant of His people He means the two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, because He had already rejected the ten tribes when Assyria took them captive. God warns Manasseh and his people with these punishments, that perhaps they may repent and He may turn back from His punishment, but sadly they did not repent.

21.13.0.en: God declares that the reason for His punishment of the kingdom of Judah is the evils it committed, from the time the people of God were in Egypt until this time, and the Bible mentions them in the books of the Kings and the Prophets, and they are:

21.13.1.en: 1- They practiced pagan worship in Jerusalem, such as bowing down on the housetops to the gods of heaven (Jer 19:13).

21.13.2.en: 2- They made cakes for the queen of heaven (Jer 7:18).

21.13.3.en: 3- They built the high places of Tophet in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in order to please the pagan gods (Jer 7:31).

21.13.4.en: 4- They built houses for the sodomites by the house of the Lord, that is, they encouraged sexual perversion (ch. 23:7).

21.13.5.en: 5- The women wove hangings for the grove (ch. 23:7), that is, for the god Ashtoreth, the goddess of love among the Phoenicians.

21.13.6.en: 6- The leaders of the people were wicked: the princes were roaring lions, devouring the people, the judges were evening wolves, the prophets were light and treacherous, and the priests polluted the sanctuary and did violence to the Law (Zeph 3:3, 4).

21.13.7.en: 7- There was iniquity in the city, and injustice, plundering, oppression and strife (Hab 1:3, 4). In sum, the people of God worshiped idols and plunged into evil lusts.

21.14.0.en: Among the evils of Manasseh is that he killed all who opposed his religious policy and all who objected to his uncleanness and evils, such as the prophet Isaiah, so that he filled Jerusalem with the blood of the innocent. Manasseh's sins were not limited to himself; all Judah turned aside after him and followed him in his errors and deviations, so he is responsible for leading them astray.

21.14.1.en: Pride is what drove Manasseh to be immersed in sin, so beware of it, because the proud person does not listen to any advice. Humble yourself before God, confess your sins before your father of confession and accept guidance, and God will deliver you from every punishment, because He loves you.

21.15.0.en: The rest of what Manasseh did and the wrong, unclean ways he followed are recorded in the "Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah." Manasseh repented after he was taken captive to Babylon, late in his life, then returned to Jerusalem and made many religious reforms, mentioned in (2 Chr 33:11-19).

21.15.1.en: The distress Manasseh went through at his captivity made him repent. So do not be disturbed by distress, because it is your way to cleaving to God, your turning back from your sins and your spiritual growth. Submit to the will of God, for He arranges every good for you.

21.16.0.en: The garden of Uzza: it is the garden of Azariah, and it is part of the royal palace.

21.16.1.en: Manasseh died and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and his son Amon reigned after him. Twenty-one kings reigned over the kingdom of Judah, and they were buried as follows:

21.16.2.en: 1- Fifteen in the city of David, which is part of Jerusalem and in which are the tombs of the kings.

21.16.3.en: 2- Two, Manasseh and his son Amon, in the garden of Uzza.

21.16.5.en: 4- Two in Babylon, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.

21.16.6.en: 5- One, Jehoiakim, whose place of burial is not known.

21.17.s.en: (4) The evils of Amon and his death

21.17.0.en: Jotbah: at present it is Khirbet Jefat, and it lies in Galilee.

21.17.1.en: Amon reigned after the death of his father Manasseh, when he was twenty-two years old, and his reign in Jerusalem lasted two years, and his mother's name was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

21.18.0.en: Amon committed the same transgressions and sins that his father Manasseh committed before he repented.

21.19.0.en: Amon walked in the ways of his father Manasseh and worshiped the idols that his father had set up. He did not humble himself, as his father Manasseh humbled himself late in his life, but increased in iniquity.

21.19.1.en: If God has put some sins far from you, do not return to renewing them and attaching yourself to their sources, for this angers God greatly. Be careful, and learn from the mistakes of others.

21.20.0.en: Amon abandoned the worship of the true God, the God of his fathers, and did not follow His ways or keep His commandments.

21.21.0.en: His servants conspired against him and rebelled against him and killed him in his house.

21.22.0.en: The rebels were planning an insurrection, but the people put it down, and the people killed all those who had rebelled against King Amon, and made his son Josiah king in his place, although he was still a child of eight, in fulfillment of the prophecies for the preservation of the house of David. Amon died a young man at the age of twenty-four, and his reign lasted only two years.

21.22.1.en: Perhaps the people rejoiced at being rid of the wicked Amon and gave no opportunity for one of his wicked servants to reign, but held fast to the word of God and made Josiah the son of Amon king in his place.

21.23.0.en: The rest of the acts of Amon and what he did during his short reign are recorded in the "Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah."

21.24.0.en: He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place. Josiah king over Judah

22.0.0.en: Boscath: it lies in the south of the kingdom of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem, near Lachish.

22.0.1.en: Josiah was eight years old when he succeeded his father Amon on the throne, and his reign lasted thirty-one years in the capital Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath, who was therefore a Jewess, not a Gentile, and most likely a godly woman, because the Bible mentions her name and immediately after it shows the uprightness of the life of her son, who reigned as a child; and most likely she took care to bring him up spiritually.

22.1.0.en: Josiah did all that was right and followed in the steps of his great forefather David, and did not turn aside from the straight path to the right or to the left. The Bible's praise of him is not repeated for the kings of Judah except for Hezekiah and Asa. Most likely Josiah's righteousness is due to the following:

22.1.1.en: 1- What he learned from his godly mother.

22.1.2.en: 2- His grandfather King Manasseh repented in the last days of his life, in about the last five years of it, and perhaps he tried to reform his son Amon, who did not respond, so he took care of his grandson Josiah, who had reached the age of six at the death of his grandfather.

22.1.3.en: 3- The presence of spiritual guides in the kingdom with Josiah, such as the prophet Jeremiah, Shaphan the scribe and the prophetess Huldah.

22.2.0.en: Shaphan: he was the scribe of King Josiah and was godly, and his sons were Ahikam, who rescued Jeremiah from the pit (Jer 26:24), and Gemariah, who was one of the counselors of King Jehoiakim and in whose chamber Baruch read the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer 36:10). The grandson of Shaphan is the righteous Gedaliah, who governed the kingdom of Judah after the Babylonian captivity and the capture of King Zedekiah.

22.2.1.en: When King Josiah reached the age of twenty-six, he began his first reforms by sending to the temple Shaphan the scribe, the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, asking him to charge Hilkiah the high priest to count the money that the people donated and that the doorkeepers collected from them, as King Joash did (ch. 12:4-14), to be given to those who oversee the work of renewing the temple, who would pay it to the workmen carrying out the repair of the ruined parts of the temple.

22.2.2.en: We notice that Jeremiah began his prophecy five years before these reforms (Jer 1:2), and perhaps it was an encouragement to Josiah to carry out these reforms.

22.2.3.en: Assyria fell in the twelfth year of Josiah, that is, six years before these reforms, and the Babylonian empire began, but Josiah did not pay attention to these political changes in the world and focused his concern on the spiritual reforms of his country.

22.3.0.en: Josiah commanded that this money be paid to the carpenters, the builders and the masons, and for buying the materials for the building, timber and hewn stone, to repair the temple. From the abundance of the works and materials that were used to repair the temple, we sense the extent of the destruction that had befallen it in the days of Manasseh, then Amon, and consequently the greatness of the reforms and repairs carried out by Josiah.

22.4.0.en: The overseers of the work of renewing the temple were not asked for an account of how the sums given to them were spent, because of their honesty, and they were Levites (2 Chr 34:12).

22.4.1.en: How beautiful it is that we care for the Church, the house of the Lord, not only by repairing her walls and caring for her buildings, but also for every service offered in her and for all souls, that they may enjoy God's care within her.

22.5.s.en: (2) The finding of the Book of the Law

22.5.0.en: While Hilkiah the priest was occupied with repairing the house of the Lord, assisted in this by the priests and Levites, he found a copy of the Book of the Law, which was most likely the five books of Moses, or at least the Book of Deuteronomy, and it had been lost amid the neglect in the days of the wicked kings. Also the former kings neglected that each should keep a copy of the Law, as God had commanded. So Hilkiah rejoiced greatly and handed this copy to Shaphan the scribe to give to the righteous King Josiah, who cared for the worship of God. Shaphan read it as soon as he received it, and this shows the extent of Shaphan's godliness and his concern for the word of God. This shows the grace of God given to His children who care for His house and His worship, for He gave them not only help in repairing the house, but also His holy word, that is, the Book of the Law. Whoever strives spiritually receives many blessings from God.

22.5.1.en: Everyone who strives spiritually and serves God faithfully, God reveals to him many secrets of His knowledge, guides him in his life and satisfies him with His love. So be a persevering striver, confident that God cares for your labor, whatever your falls and weakness.

22.6.0.en: Shaphan returned to the king to tell him that his orders for repairing the temple were being carried out, for the chest in which the people entering the house of the Lord put silver had already been emptied (ch. 12:9), and the money was counted and paid to the overseers in charge of repairing the house, to be spent on the workmen.

22.7.0.en: Shaphan also told the king that Hilkiah the high priest had given him a book, the Book of the Law, which Hilkiah had found while the temple was being repaired, and then Shaphan read it before the king.

22.7.1.en: Shaphan mentions that it was a book because the Book of the Law was not known to the king and the people at this time; they had forgotten it because of the departure of Manasseh and Amon from God, a period of nearly sixty years, that is, not a short period, after King Hezekiah. This shows how far the people of God had departed from His holy word.

22.8.0.en: When King Josiah heard the words of the Book of the Law, which Shaphan read to him, he believed everything in it and discovered his sins and the sins of his people, and feared God's punishment because of the multitude of their sins (Deut 28:16-68, Lev 26:14-39). He grieved in holy repentance, to the point that he tore his clothes in remorse before God. The tearing of clothes was a well-known eastern custom showing intense grief. It is noticeable that Shaphan, despite his godliness, did not tear his clothes when he read the book before the high priest or before the king, and this shows the depth of the repentance of the righteous Josiah.

22.9.0.en: Josiah was not content to be moved by the word of God, but took practical steps for repentance. He gathered his godly counselors, namely Hilkiah the high priest, Shaphan the scribe and his son Ahikam, and two of those close to him, Achbor and Asaiah. And he said to them: Seek for me a prophet, to make known to me and my people the word of God and its interpretation, and to pray for us and guide us how to obey the word of God, that we may be saved from His wrath and not walk in the way of our fathers, who neglected the word of God and His worship and worshiped idols. By this he means the period in which Manasseh and Amon reigned.

22.10.0.en: The godly envoys of the king searched for a prophet of God to inform them and make them understand the words of the Law, and they found the prophetess Huldah, who lived in Jerusalem, in the second quarter of it, that is, the new quarter, which is different from the first, the old quarter, in which the city of David is. She was the wife of Shallum, who was in charge of guarding the priests' garments in the house of the Lord and any other garments kept in the temple. Huldah lived in her home, exercising her ministry in the area around her, and did not travel about like some prophets, such as Elisha and Isaiah. Among the blessings of God at this time is the presence of other prophets (ch. 23:2) to proclaim His voice in the days of the wicked kings Manasseh and Amon and to support the righteous King Josiah, and among these prophets was the prophetess Huldah. This means that God gives prophecy to men and women, although He gives it more to men, that they may move and travel in different places to proclaim His voice.

22.11.0.en: The prophetess Huldah declared the voice of God to the king's envoys, that they might convey it to him, namely that the punishments mentioned in the Book of the Law would come upon this place, that is, the kingdom of Judah and all who are in it. The reason for God's wrath and these punishments is His people's worship of idols and their forsaking of Him, and the divine punishment would continue for a long time. This is what happened in the destruction and burning of Jerusalem and the captivity that lasted seventy years.

22.12.0.en: After the prophetess Huldah declared God's judgment concerning the kingdom of Judah, she gave the second message to King Josiah, who had cared to hear the word of God when Shaphan the scribe read it to him, and was deeply moved and repented of his sins and those of his people when he heard of the punishment coming upon all. God's word to him was: I have heard your prayers and your weeping and your tender heart humbled before Me; therefore this punishment will not happen in your days, and you will depart in peace from this world and be buried with your fathers, because of your repentance and humility. So the king's envoys returned to him and told him the word of God that the prophetess Huldah had declared.

22.12.1.en: Josiah died at Megiddo, during the war into which he put himself without need, because it was a war between Egypt and Assyria; and they buried him with his fathers, the kings of Judah, in Jerusalem, and he did not see the punishment of Jerusalem in his days, for this happened in the days of his son Zedekiah, when the Babylonian captivity took place. Thus the righteous Josiah lived in peace, he and his country, all his days.

22.12.2.en: Your repentance changes everything and removes the wrath of God from you, so He wipes out your sins and every punishment, supports you and rejoices in you, and you live anew and enjoy fellowship with Him. So hasten to repentance, however great your sins or however often repeated.

22.12.3.en: The reforms of Josiah and the reigns of his sons Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
